doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Milt Jackson's Goodbye
summary: Brown names the Milt Jackson CTI quintet date; Laws can't recall it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Again, 333 sessions. That’s completely understandable. But from our perspective, the fans, when we – budding students, we’re keeping our ear to the ground, if you’re playing flute. I have to put a footnote to that one. The next one is Milt Jackson, Goodbye, for CTI, small group, quintet, with Cedar, yourself, Ron Carter, Steve Gadd. Milt Jackson. We talked about Bobby. How about back to Bags?
You know what? As I recall, I don’t remember him being there when I did my part. I think – is Don Sebesky arrangement on that?
It doesn’t give an arranging credit. It’s a quintet.
I know later on when he did Sunflower, I think that’s – I’m sure Don came and did those arrangements.
I just don’t recall that session.
